title: A finite-type subalgebra of a normal domain has a normal finite-type extension inside it
statement: Let R be an integrally closed integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and C a finitely generated Z-subalgebra of R [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then there is a Z-subalgebra A of R containing C, finitely generated over Z, and integrally closed in its own fraction field. No algebraicity assumption on R over C is imposed. All rings have the universe of R.

source.place: Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), third paragraph; details of the normalization and directed-union construction

proof.text: Let K be the fraction field of C and N its integral closure in K. Since C is finite type over Z, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-domain-normalization-finite] gives Module.Finite C N. A module-finite algebra is finite type, and finite type is transitive, so N is finite type over Z.

The normalization N is an integrally closed domain by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal], applied to the trivial extension of K. In Lean use integralClosure.isIntegrallyClosedOfFiniteExtension K.

Embed K in L=Frac(R) by the injective inclusion of C into R. Restrict this map to N. Each image is integral over C and then over R, so lies in the image of R in L because R is integrally closed. Codomain-restrict to that image and invert the isomorphism R to its image to obtain an injective integer-algebra map h:N to R.

Take A=h.range. The image contains C because h agrees with the inclusion on C. The isomorphism N to A transfers integral closure, while the surjection N to A transfers finite type over Z. Convert finite type to Subalgebra.FG. This proves all three assertions.
